name: VS Code + Copilot
description: GitHub Copilot integrated directly into the Visual Studio Code editor. Behavior is scoped through .vscode/ workspace settings, repository instruction files (AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md), and the open VS Code workspace/folder. Agent mode (GA 2025) turns Copilot into an autonomous, multi-step coding agent that reads files, edits code, runs terminal commands, and uses MCP tools. A 2025 'Agent HQ'/unified Agent Sessions surface adds parallel local, background (CLI), and cloud agents with handoffs.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Required GitHub account, federated via OAuth in the editor ('Sign in to GitHub'). Using Copilot in VS Code requires an active Copilot plan: Copilot Free (limited completions/chat for individuals), or paid Pro / Pro+ / Max for personal use, or Copilot Business / Enterprise seats assigned by an org (Business/Enterprise seats are not eligible for the Free tier). Auth is to GitHub.com by default; GHE.com/GitHub Enterprise Server can be configured (a common source of sign-in failures). There is no anonymous/device-local mode for Copilot itself — VS Code is free and works offline, but Copilot features need a signed-in Copilot-entitled GitHub identity. The editor itself binds settings/identity to the local OS user profile.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: VS Code is a single-user desktop editor — there is no shared live workspace inside the editor (Live Share is a separate product). Multi-user/org governance comes from GitHub: Copilot Business/Enterprise admins control feature rollout and policy (e.g. via the Policies page and enterprise AI settings), and org-level custom instructions are automatically detected and applied to all of a member's chat requests across repos. Team sharing of context happens through version-controlled files committed to the repo (.vscode/settings.json, AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*, .github/agents/*.agent.md) rather than a hosted teamspace. When work is delegated to the cloud coding agent, collaboration reverts to standard GitHub PR review flows (branch protections, CODEOWNERS, required reviews apply).

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A 'workspace' is the VS Code workspace: either a single open folder (typically one git repo) or a multi-root workspace defined by a .code-workspace file listing multiple folders. It maps to filesystem paths on disk, not an abstract cloud entity. The workspace is the unit that scopes settings (.vscode/settings.json), trust, instruction files, and the context Copilot indexes. For monorepos, multi-root .code-workspace files plus settings like scoping completions to the active folder bound Copilot's context to a single service/subfolder rather than the whole tree. There is no separate hosted workspace object — the open folder(s) on disk IS the workspace.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Chat/agent sessions are bound to the open workspace and stored under that workspace's storage (VS Code workspaceStorage/[hash]/chatSessions/*.json). A user can run multiple chat/agent sessions simultaneously within one workspace and track them in the unified Agent Sessions view; in 2025, local agent sessions remain active in the background even after the chat window is closed (earlier behavior cancelled them). Sessions are also viewable per-project in the sessions list and can be resumed. Copilot CLI maintains its own parallel sessions (in ~/.copilot/session-state/) that can be surfaced inside VS Code. So binding is primarily workspace-scoped, with the user's GitHub identity as the auth boundary; cloud-agent sessions delegated out of the editor are repo-scoped on GitHub.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Workspace/repo-level context: the open folder(s) contents, .vscode/settings.json (Copilot enable/disable per language, chat.disableAIFeatures, tool/agent settings), instruction files (AGENTS.md root or nested, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with applyTo globs), .copilotignore (exclude generated/fixture files), prompt files, custom agents (.github/agents/*.agent.md), and Agent Skills (SKILL.md folders auto-loaded when relevant). User/global level: personal custom instructions and user settings in the user profile. Org level: organization-wide custom instructions auto-detected and applied to all chat requests. Session level: the conversation/prompt text, attached files/#-references, and the agent's tool-execution log. Tool context is extended per-workspace/user via MCP servers and extensions (subject to trust/approval).
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Multiple instruction sources are ALL supplied to the model; on conflict, higher priority wins. Priority order: (1) personal/user-level instructions (highest), then (2) repository instructions. Repository instruction files: .github/copilot-instructions.md (repo-wide, recommended concise, ~under 1000 words); AGENTS.md (root or nested anywhere in the tree — the NEAREST AGENTS.md to the worked-on file takes precedence among agent-instruction files; can substitute for copilot-instructions.md); .github/instructions/*.instructions.md (path-specific, applied when the worked-on file matches the applyTo glob, with an excludeAgent property to hide a file from a specific agent such as code-review); CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are also read for cross-tool compatibility. Org-level instructions layer in via the Chat Instructions menu. Agent Skills (SKILL.md) are loaded contextually when relevant. There is no single documented hard byte cap, but copilot-instructions.md is recommended to stay short.
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not a curated-document research corpus. Grounding is the code in the open workspace/repo (workspace indexing, file references, #-mentions, and Copilot's codebase search), optionally extended by MCP servers/tools and committed instruction files. There is no NotebookLM/Perplexity-Space-style bounded upload set; 'sources' are the files on disk plus whatever MCP tools can reach. .copilotignore and active-folder scoping narrow which files are considered.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Local-first. Chat/agent session state is stored on disk in VS Code's per-workspace storage: workspaceStorage/[hash]/chatSessions/*.json (JSON session files keyed by a workspace hash). Settings persist as JSON (.vscode/settings.json per-workspace, user settings.json globally). Instruction/config files persist in the repo (Markdown, version-controlled via git). Copilot CLI sessions persist separately under ~/.copilot/session-state/ (plus a cloud session store). State is mutable/snapshot-style (session JSON files updated in place) rather than an append-only event log. Cloud-delegated coding-agent runs persist their durable output as GitHub Git artifacts (branch/PR/commits/logs), not locally.
persistence_and_history.session_history: Conversations are stored as local JSON files per workspace and browsable in the editor (Chat view history, and the unified Agent Sessions list showing status across local/background/cloud agents). Sessions can be saved, exported (to share or reuse), archived/marked done (moved out of the active list), or permanently deleted (irreversible). Because they live as JSON on disk they are portable — users transfer Copilot chat history between devices by copying the workspaceStorage chatSessions files. Notably, VS Code Copilot Chat history is currently siloed from the Copilot CLI /chronicle history even on the same machine/repo. Retention is effectively until the user deletes (or VS Code clears workspace storage). [uncertain] Exact JSON schema/versioning and any automatic pruning policy are not formally documented.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Durable, user-authored layer = instruction files (AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md, path-specific instructions, prompt files, Agent Skills) committed to the repo and applied on every relevant request, plus user-level personal and org-level instructions. Ephemeral per-session layer = the chat conversation/context window and the agent's tool-execution log, stored in the session JSON. Context can be condensed via a 'Compact conversation' action. There is no first-class automatic semantic long-term memory store comparable to Windsurf memories or Claude auto-memory; cross-session 'memory' is achieved by writing knowledge into the version-controlled instruction files (a deliberate, reviewable bridge from experience to durable config). Checkpoints add a session-scoped restore layer (below).
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: Within the editor, prior sessions are browsable via the Chat history and the Agent Sessions list (status, switch between, resume). Retrieval is primarily navigational (pick a session / fork from a checkpoint) rather than a global full-text/semantic search index across all past conversations. The Copilot CLI offers a session picker (--resume / --continue). [uncertain] Whether VS Code provides full-text or semantic search ACROSS all stored chatSessions JSON files (versus listing/opening them) is not clearly documented; cross-workspace search of history is not a documented first-class feature.
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Local sessions persist on disk until the user deletes them, archives them, or VS Code clears the workspace storage (e.g. workspace removed). No documented TTL/auto-expiry for local Copilot chat sessions. Checkpoints provide intra-session lifecycle control: a checkpoint rolls back BOTH file changes and chat history to a point in the conversation (enabled by default via chat.checkpoints.enabled), and editing a previous request reverts that and all subsequent changes. Forking a checkpoint creates a new session containing only requests up to that point. Cloud-delegated runs use ephemeral environments destroyed at end (durable artifacts kept on GitHub). [uncertain] A documented checkpoint-restore + 'Compact conversation' state-sync bug could wipe chat history in some 2025 versions.

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: Local agent mode executes in the user's real workspace by default (it edits files and runs terminal commands on the local machine), gated by Workspace Trust (untrusted/Restricted Mode disables code-executing features) and explicit per-tool approval (every non-read-only tool/terminal call requires approval; approvals can be granted per session, per workspace, or always). A 2025 preview adds OS-level Agent Sandboxing for terminal commands (runInTerminal): kernel-enforced file-system and network boundaries — read access limited to workspace folders + sandbox temp (home dir reads denied to protect SSH keys/shell config/credentials), writes limited to the working directory and subdirectories. MCP servers/extensions run with broad machine access and are governed by trust prompts (VS Code prompts before trusting workspaces, extensions, MCP servers, and network domains). Stronger isolation options: run the agent in a Dev Container, or use Git Worktree isolation (notably for Copilot CLI sessions) so agent changes land in a separate worktree folder. Network is on by default for the editor; the cloud coding agent (separate) runs in an isolated GitHub Actions environment with a default egress firewall.
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: No first-class machine/environment snapshot in the local editor — there is no save/restore of installed packages or env vars as a unit. The closest mechanisms are: (a) chat Checkpoints, which restore workspace FILE changes (and chat) to a conversation point (session-scoped, not a full env snapshot); (b) Git itself for file/branch state; (c) reproducible environments via Dev Containers / devcontainer.json or, for the cloud agent, copilot-setup-steps.yml. So 'restore' of environment is achieved by version-controlled re-provisioning rather than binary snapshots. [uncertain] No documented persistence of an agent's installed-tool state across sessions beyond what git/dev-container config captures.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Yes — a defining 2025 capability. From the Chat view a local agent session can be continued as a background (Copilot CLI) or cloud (Copilot Coding Agent) session via a 'Continue in' option; the entire chat context is passed to the cloud agent and the original local session is archived. The Plan agent can 'Continue in Cloud' to run an implementation plan; a background session can hand off with /delegate. Cloud results return as branches/PRs reviewable in the editor. Direction is primarily local->background->cloud (with results pulled back via git); there is no live in-memory migration of a running process, but chat context is preserved across the handoff. VS Code itself is local/desktop (self-hostable as your own machine); the cloud agent runtime is GitHub-hosted and not self-hostable.
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: Strong in 2025 'Agent HQ'. The unified Agent Sessions view ('mission control') runs and tracks multiple agent sessions in parallel across local, background (CLI), and cloud, with per-session status, file-change review, and resume. Background agents run in isolated workspaces so they don't interfere with active work; multiple Copilot CLI sessions can run in parallel. Subagents are context-isolated: a main agent delegates work and only the final result flows back (intermediate exploration stays contained), and multiple subagents can run in parallel (faster results, fewer premium requests). Custom agents support handoffs (e.g. Plan -> Implement -> Review) via frontmatter, and a coordinator can fan out subtasks. Isolation between parallel sessions is by separate workspaces/worktrees/branches. [uncertain] Exact concurrency caps (bounded by premium-request quota and machine/Actions limits) are not fixed numbers.
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Primarily the VS Code editor: Chat view (Ask/Edit/Agent modes), the Agent Sessions view, inline chat, and command palette. Extended surfaces in 2025: Copilot CLI sessions launched/managed from within VS Code (background, local machine); delegation to the GitHub-hosted Copilot Coding Agent (which is itself also triggerable by assigning a GitHub Issue, from github.com, GitHub CLI, JetBrains/Eclipse, Raycast, and external tools like Jira/Linear/Slack/Teams). Within the editor, sessions are user-initiated by typing a prompt or running an agent; there is no in-editor cron trigger. Each model request to an agent/cloud surface consumes premium requests.

implementation.implementation_stack: Client: VS Code (Electron/TypeScript desktop editor) + the open-source-ish GitHub Copilot Chat extension (microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat). Auth: GitHub OAuth in-editor; org/enterprise policy gating via GitHub. Local persistence: JSON files in VS Code workspaceStorage/[hash]/chatSessions/*.json for chat/agent sessions; settings as JSON (.vscode/settings.json workspace, user settings.json global); Copilot CLI sessions under ~/.copilot/session-state/. Config: Markdown instruction files (AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md, CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md), custom agents .github/agents/*.agent.md (YAML frontmatter), Agent Skills (SKILL.md). Tools: MCP servers/extensions, gated by Workspace Trust + per-tool approval + preview OS-level Agent Sandboxing (kernel FS/network isolation for terminal commands). Isolation options: Dev Containers, Git Worktrees. Cloud delegation: GitHub Copilot Coding Agent on GitHub Actions-backed ephemeral Linux with egress firewall, persisting branch/PR/commits/session-logs as Git artifacts. Models: GPT/Claude/Gemini families selectable. [uncertain] Internal session-JSON schema and backend orchestration details are not fully documented.
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: VS Code + Copilot is the 'local-first, filesystem-scoped, instruction-cascade' archetype and offers several mappings for Labmate. (1) Identity: required federated identity (GitHub OAuth) with org policy gating — Labmate can mirror by binding sessions to the Discord connector identity as the user key and gating features by org/workspace policy. (2) Workspace = on-disk folder vs Labmate's abstract workspace_id: Labmate should keep the abstract workspace_id (like Claude Projects) rather than a filesystem path, but can borrow the multi-root/active-folder SCOPING idea to bound retrieval to a sub-corpus within a workspace. (3) Instruction precedence: the clean cascade — personal/user > repository instructions, with NEAREST AGENTS.md winning and path-glob applyTo files — is a directly adoptable precedence model for workspace_id-scoped vs global vs path/topic-scoped instructions stored in MongoDB. (4) Persistence: local JSON-per-session (workspaceStorage/[hash]/chatSessions) parallels Labmate storing one session document per thread; the hash-keyed-by-workspace layout maps to indexing session docs by workspace_id. (5) Lifecycle: Checkpoints (restore BOTH file state and chat history to a conversation point, plus fork) suggest Labmate could checkpoint LangGraph thread state for rollback/branching; the 'Compact conversation' idea maps to summarizing Redis-held active state to control context size. (6) Memory: knowledge lives in version-controlled instruction files rather than auto-memory — Labmate can keep durable user-authored workspace instructions in MongoDB and treat Redis Streams as the ephemeral per-session layer. (7) Parallelism/handoff: the Agent HQ pattern (parallel local/background/cloud sessions, context-isolated subagents, local->cloud handoff passing full chat context, results returned as artifacts) is a strong template for Labmate fanning out subagents that return only final results while the coordinator's context stays clean, and for handing a Discord-initiated session to a heavier background worker while preserving thread_id context. (8) Safety defaults: Workspace Trust + per-tool approval + OS-level sandbox (home-dir reads denied, writes confined to working dir) are concrete defaults to emulate for any Labmate tool-execution path.
